mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain stuck near their current depressed levels, weekday trip chaining stays weak and retail visits do not recover, so RETAIL_REC stays below the last four-week mean over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises above its last 28-day mean while WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remain within 5 points of their current averages.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week jump in PARKS use pulls discretionary outings away from retail and recreation for the next one to two weeks, depressing RETAIL_REC when park mobility is materially higher than its recent average.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within the next 7-14 days after a PARKS increase of more than 5 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: When TRANSIT recovers enough to move materially above its current baseline, access friction to shopping districts falls and retail-and-recreation mobility increases over the following month.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -45 and stays there for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its prior four-week mean within 28 days after TRANSIT crosses above -45 for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: A combined rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT creates commuting-linked retail demand: the interaction matters because retail gains only appear when both mobility streams improve together, not when either one rises alone.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both rise by at least 3 points from their current weekly means.

mechanism_narrative: If RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while GROCERY_PHARM remains suppressed, households are substituting toward at-home routines and away from shopping trips, which keeps RETAIL_REC below the previous month’s average.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 28 days despite RESIDENTIAL staying above 13 and GROCERY_PHARM staying below -20 on average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PARKS and a simultaneous easing of RESIDENTIAL time indicate favorable outdoor conditions and lower stay-at-home intensity, which should lift retail and recreation visits over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL falls from the current week by at least 4 points each
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve within 14 days after PARKS rises and RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 4 points from their current levels.

mechanism_narrative: Under a tightening-restrictions regime, further drops in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES will mechanically suppress discretionary shopping trips, making RETAIL_REC lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:current mobility remains heavily negative across transit and workplaces
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall relative to the prior 28-day mean even as TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both remain at or below current levels.

mechanism_narrative: Because GROCERY_PHARM is less depressed than retail right now, a short-term substitution effect can emerge: when grocery trips ease, some foot traffic shifts back to retail and recreation within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 3 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 7 days after GROCERY_PHARM improves by at least 3 points week-on-week.
